traits.hypanthium.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 320, 321: Simpson describes the flowers as hypogynous or perigynous and his family formula ends 'hypanthium sometimes present' (e.g. Cercis, the mimosoid clade).

traits.note: Jepson's Manual of the Flowering Plants of California (1925), read in full, as Leguminosae: calyx synsepalous, 5-toothed or cleft; corolla of 5 petals, regular or somewhat irregular or commonly papilionaceous (so symmetry is each genus's); stamens 10, monadelphous, diadelphous or distinct (Acacia numerous); pistil 1, superior, 1-celled.

traits.leaf_division.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), families 27 Caesalpiniaceae and 28 Mimosaceae, which APG joins with his Papilionaceae as Fabaceae: leaves pinnate or bipinnate, rarely simple or of one leaflet; fruit a legume or one that does not split.

traits.fruit_type.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), families 27 Caesalpiniaceae and 28 Mimosaceae, which APG joins with his Papilionaceae as Fabaceae: leaves pinnate or bipinnate, rarely simple or of one leaflet; fruit a legume or one that does not split.

traits.stipules.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA), Leguminosae: leaves nearly always with stipules, sometimes spiny; without them in under 2% (some Mirbelieae).

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA), Leguminosae: leaves usually alternate; opposite or whorled in under 1% (some Mirbelieae).

traits.division_pattern.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA), Leguminosae: leaves commonly compound, then commonly pinnate or bipinnate, also ternate, palmate, one- or two-foliolate.

traits.sexual_system.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA), Leguminosae: plants mostly with bisexual flowers (Caesalpinioideae and Papilionoideae); some monoecious, andromonoecious or polygamomonoecious, unisexual flowers commoner in the Mimosoideae.

rules.note: How the herb program draws a palmate leaf from a flora's petiole and leaflet lengths, a choice of the model's (spec rework E4): its card is the petiole and a leaflet end to end, so the leaf is as long as both and the petiole's share is its length over theirs.

generator.params.leaf_length.why: A palmate leaf is its petiole and a leaflet end to end, so a herb's longest leaf is as long as its flora's petioles and leaflets together.

generator.params.basal_length.why: A palmate basal leaf is its petiole and a leaflet end to end, as a stem leaf is.

appearance.organs.*.shape.petiole.why: A palmate leaf's card is its petiole and a leaflet end to end, so the petiole's share is its length over theirs together.
